speaker: SPEAKER_00
transcript: Well, certainly I've been deeply involved in analyzing what the governor is proposing. I think it's important to note that this is a proposal by the governor. It's not the governor that writes the budget. The legislature writes the budget and the governor either approves by citing the budget bill or disapproves by vetoing the budget bill. But that's the way that the process is supposed to work. Certainly we all have faced a monumental challenge in balancing the budget this year. Unlike the federal government, we do not have the option of deficit spending. We can't run a structural deficit. Our Constitution requires us to pass a balanced budget every year, which means that we have to deal with this revenue shortfall. So the projected revenue shortfall is about a third of overall state revenues. In response to that, the governor is proposing about a 9% reduction in state expenditures. And he's plugging the rest of the holes with some tactics that I agree with, normally, namely using some of our budget reserve funds. We're using almost $8 billion from the BSA, what we call our rainy day fund. We're using another billion dollars from our safety net reserve accounts and public school stabilization accounts. So that's appropriate. I also think it's appropriate that we're only using less than half of those reserves. That's an acknowledgement of the fact that this is going to be a multi-year budget problem. In other words, we're not just going to have to face this this year. I think that the legislature is going to be in the same situation next year. as we're struggling to get our stimulus going and our economy moving again. However, the governor is doing some things that I very much disagree with to balance this budget. I think it's very important that we're the adults in the room. We have to face the situation head on. And although the cuts are painful, I think that they need to be made. in a way that doesn't kick the can down the road. And in a couple of instances, the governor is using what I call gimmicks, budgetary gimmicks to balance the budget. And I'll give you a couple of examples. First of all, he's proposing over $10 billion in inner fund borrowing. And what that is, is we have a lot of funds within the Department of Finance that are what we call encumbered. So they can only be used for specific purposes. They cannot be used for general purposes. So what the governor is proposing to do is to borrow money from those funds, transfer them into the general fund, and then sign a document that says that later, the state will pay those funds back from the general fund with interest.
